title: Exclusive-or form of negated identification
statement: Let $n,m\ge 0$, let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, let $z\in\{0,1\}^n$, and let $\pi:[n]\to[m]$. For every $w\in\{0,1\}^m$, the negated coordinate identification satisfies $g(w)=f(z\oplus(w_{\pi(i)})_{i=1}^n)$, where $\oplus$ is coordinatewise addition modulo two.
replaced:
For every $n,m\in\mathbb N$, $f:\{0,1\}^{n}\to\mathbb R$, $z\in\{0,1\}^{n}$, $w\in\{0,1\}^{m}$ and map $\pi:\{1,\ldots,n\}\to\{1,\ldots,m\}$, define $g(v)=f((u_i(v))_{i=1}^{n})$, where $u_i(v)=1-v_{\pi(i)}$ when $z_i=1$ and $u_i(v)=v_{\pi(i)}$ when $z_i=0$; then
\[
g(w)=f\bigl(z\oplus(w_{\pi(i)})_{i=1}^{n}\bigr),
\]
where $\oplus$ is coordinatewise addition modulo $2$.
